title: $E$-coefficient smooth base change
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, let $A=\mathcal O_E$ and fix a uniformizer $\varpi$. Consider a cartesian square [sbc-def-base-change-square]
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Y&\xrightarrow{h}&X\\
e\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
T&\xrightarrow{g}&S.
\end{array}
$$
Assume that $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, all four schemes are noetherian, $X$ and $T$ have finite dimension, and $\ell$ is invertible on $S$. For each corner $W$, let $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(W,A)$ denote the full category of derived-complete complexes of modules over the completed coefficient sheaf $A_W$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], and define
$$D_{\mathrm{comp}}(W,E)=D_{\mathrm{comp}}(W,A)[1/\varpi]$$
by raw scalar localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. For $W=X,T$, use $\Dbc(W,E)=\Dbc(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)[1/\varpi]$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Rational completed pullback and direct image mean the scalar localizations of the corresponding integral completed functors [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; their exchange is the scalar localization of the integral completed exchange.

Let $K_E\in\Dbc(T,E)$ admit a finite-level etale admissible lattice $L$ with a specified isomorphism $\iota:L[1/\varpi]\xrightarrow{\sim}K_E$ [sbc-def-admissible-lattices]. Then the exchange morphism is an isomorphism
$$
Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}Rg_{*,\mathrm{comp},E}K_E
\xrightarrow{\sim}
Rh_{*,\mathrm{comp},E}Le^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}K_E
\quad\text{in }D_{\mathrm{comp}}(X,E).
$$
Its value at $K_E$, transported using $\iota$, is independent of the chosen admissible lattice and its presentation. If the lattice is square-constructibly admissible [sbc-def-admissible-lattices], this is an isomorphism in $\Dbc(X,E)$.

proof.text: Map the unit ell in global sections along each structure morphism and then each germ to obtain unit scalars on every stalk. The extension-integers DVR theorem puts ell in the maximal ideal, generated by the chosen uniformizer. Hence ell^(n+1) vanishes in A/(uniformizer^(n+1)). Its finite additive group, expressed multiplicatively, is an ell-group. Mathlib IsPGroup.exists_card_eq gives its cardinal as ell^d; its order is therefore a unit in global sections of all four corners. This avoids computing the precise residue-field degree and does not require reconstructing a perfect quotient resolution.

source.place: Opening coefficient checks; nilpotence and the finite additive ell-group give the needed order

proof.text: Finite-level etale admissibility supplies a fixed-coefficient origin of each lattice reduction. Apply pbcDerivedFunctionRealization to its isomorphism and compose with the counit of that equivalence. These are precisely the ring-sheaf origin hypotheses of adicSmoothBaseChange. Apply that theorem with the units from step 1 to obtain invertibility of the specified integral exchange and retain its conditional constructible-landing assertion.

source.place: Application of the adic theorem to the lattice

proof.text: The published rational exchange at the localized lattice is definitionally the localization functor applied to the integral exchange. Functors preserve isomorphisms. Naturality of the rational exchange along the specified lattice presentation identifies its conjugate with the component at K. This proves invertibility at K and equality with sbcTransportedExchange. Apply the same naturality identity to any other lattice presentation to prove independence.

source.place: Central localization and independence of the specified presentation

proof.text: To translate the four finite systems, use the exact coefficient view: restrict function coefficients along pbcLevelConstantComparison and then to constant scalars. The comparison normalizations show that its composite with pbcFunctionRealization is the identity, by the associated-module-sheaf unit and pbcAssociatedRestriction_exists. Thus its derived functor is isomorphic to the inverse of pbcDerivedFunctionRealization. The private constant-scalar encodings of pullback and direct image in PbcFinitePullbackConstructibility, together with ring-sheaf change, identify the ordinary operations in this view with fixed-coefficient upperStar and lowerStar. Derive these isomorphisms: exact functors commute with derivation, an equivalence preserves K-injectives, and postcomposition by an exact functor commutes with right derivation. The existing finiteCoefficientRealization_directImage and realization unit identify the witness direct image with R lowerStar; the definition of witness pullback and the two realization units identify it with derived upperStar. Consequently the same view intertwines both actual finite operations with both witness operations.

source.place: Final four-system clause: comparison of the fixed and ring-sheaf finite presentations

proof.text: An exact coefficient view commutes with homology. Fixed-coefficient intrinsic constructibility gives finite constant models on each stratum, by finite_models_of_fixed_lisse. The coefficientConstructible_iff helper identifies these with constructibility in the constant-ring module presentation. Transport along the homology comparisons; faithfulness of scalar restriction reflects the zero-object condition. Apply the operation comparisons from step 4 successively to Rg_*, Lf* Rg_*, Le*, and Rh_* Le*. The one common interval in square-constructible admissibility therefore supplies exactly the four-system hypothesis of the adic theorem, with the same endpoints and all positive levels.

source.place: Final four-system clause: transfer of constructibility and the common vanishing interval

proof.text: Use the retained landing clause of adicSmoothBaseChange to regard the two actual integral outputs as objects J and J-prime of the full constructible subcategory. Its specified exchange is an isomorphism there. Apply pbcRationalization to this isomorphism. The inclusion into the ambient raw localization commutes with localization on morphisms, by LinearMap.baseChange_tmul. Finally compose the endpoint identifications with the given lattice presentation; naturality of the rational exchange yields exactly the equation in SbcConstructibleExchangeRepresentation.

source.place: Final clause: the specified localized constructible exchange represents the ambient exchange

proof_origin.place: Coefficient ell-group arithmetic; adic exchange; explicit finite-presentation and homology comparisons; rational naturality and constructible representation.

citers.note: The input explicitly assumes the E-coefficient hypotheses at each finite stage, so finite dimensionality of X and T is inherited. Its displayed output is nevertheless D_comp(S, Qbar_ell), whereas both composites land on X. The citer requires its own output-category correction S to X. Its proof also claims coefficient-change compatibility not asserted by the E-coefficient theorem alone; that obligation must be audited in its own split.

old_proof.text:
The two-term free resolution
$[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\varpi^{n+1}}\mathcal O_E]$ of $A_n$ and
the adic theorem [sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change] give the
statement for integral lattices; central localization (inverting
multiplication by $\varpi$) of
[def-weil-pbc-rational-category] gives
it for $K_E$, independent of the admissible lattice, and the
constructible landing is the four-system hypothesis of
[sbc-def-admissible-lattices].

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N6-48ff7ffad (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read every step of the item and the full statements of all 9 proof dependencies. I also read the main-20261015 blueprint statement and proof, plus the unit sk-thm-sbc-coefficients. The delivery creates no new nodes, and step uses match proof_deps exactly. The statement is unchanged; the inherited correction from S to X is right, tested on S=T=Spec k, X=Y=A^1_k. Step 1: from the DVR lemma and the finite-quotient leaf, A_n=A/ϖ^{n+1} has a two-term free resolution, ℓ=uϖ^r with r>0, and |A_n|=ℓ^{d(n+1)}, which is invertible on every corner. These are exactly the adic datum and adic-theorem hypotheses. Step 2: the finite-level étale admissibility of sbc-def-admissible-lattices matches the input of sbc-thm-adic-smooth-base-change word for word (same A_n indexing and same completed coefficient sheaf). Step 3 uses that theorem's statement only. Steps 4–5: the helper's linearity and naturality identity give G_E(a⊗c)Q(α_L)=Q(α_L')F_E(a⊗c), and the rational exchange is by definition Q of the helper's mate. Step 6: naturality at the presentation i, then the u=(i')^{-1}i cancellation, gives invertibility at K_E and independence of the lattice. Step 7: the four-system square-admissibility condition is exactly the hypothesis of the adic theorem's final clause. Since Dbc is a full subcategory, Q(α_L) is an isomorphism in Dbc(X,E), identified with the exchange through the endpoint identifications. This essential-image reading is the only meaningful one, matches the stage-2 Lean record, and does not weaken the statement. Edge cases checked: n=0, ramified E, the zero complex, the identity square, and non-integral rational re-presentations. The route follows the blueprint proof in order. Accepted tool_uses: lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr and lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients (the latter a Mathlib leaf), both used only to check coefficient hypotheses. No SGA source is cited. For the maintainer: the item's own tool_uses and reviewed fields are left over from the old nine-step split and still list nodes it no longer uses; the unit binding sk-rem-rest differs from main-20261015's sk-thm-sbc-coefficients; and the existing node def-pc-perfect-ring-complex cites Tag 0A1U where the definition is Tag 0657. None of these is in this delivery's files, and I made no fixes.
